text: Two hundred "tests", each one is green;
The finest score you've ever seen!
My "tests"? I paste app code in haste:
A perfect duplication!
The sums agree! How sweet for me!
A shared miscalculation.
With screenshots, commas cause such dramas:
A red notification.
My "test"? Fantastic, automatic—
I change its expectation!
To boost my score, I cover more;
They've trained me just to make the grade.
Like kids in class, I aim to pass;
The marks decide how tests get made.
Did you actually test it?
Press it, stress it, second-guess it!
Find a clue? Congratulations!
Now pursue its implications.
What did you try? What did you find?
What did you try?
What did you find?
What changed your mind?
The gym? No net. We log a set;
The app says "Saved!"—but what's in store?
Reload the screen; no set is seen.
Connect once more: still gone? Explore!
We chase the clue; try something new:
Connect, then save; the sets all stay.
We drop the net, then save a set;
A new check flags what went away.

A fresh bot crew? Here's what to do:
Real browsers, a playbook, and users in mind.
The goals you name will guide the game;
Your oracles help them to judge what they find.
One probes the chat—just me and Pat:
Does Sam's new account show the text Pat just sent?
One tests the cart, then hits restart:
Do orders still match what the customer spent?
We trade the news, compare the views;
We share the doubts and observations.
Some calls need you. We'll talk them through;
We ask for fresh interpretations.
A check applies a rule we've set;
It tells us if that rule is met.
To test, we ask what else—and why;
Each clue can change what next we try.
A check reports, "The sums agree!"
We test: "Could both be wrong? Let's see!"
The checks are part of how we test;
We judge what serves the users best.

Who sees the logs? Not tested yet.
